name: TextKit 2 (NSTextLayoutManager)
verdict_reason: Apple presents TextKit 2's viewport-based, always noncontiguous layout as fast for documents of hundreds of megabytes but publishes no numbers. The one public benchmark suite found it only 'a small amount faster' than TextKit 1 on a macOS 14 beta, and a long-time TextKit 2 editor author reports unstable height estimates and scrolling jumps.
tier_reason: Directional statements only: Apple gives no figures and the third-party benchmark README reports results in words.
claimed_speedup: No numbers. Apple: 'TextKit 2 is extremely fast'. ChimeHQ TextViewBenchmark: TextKit 2 'even a small amount faster' than TextKit 1 on a macOS 14 beta; TextKit 2 was 'basically unusable' on macOS 12.
workload: Apple: scrolling and laying out large documents. ChimeHQ: automated XCTest UI performance tests of NSTextView on macOS.
one_liner: Apple's viewport-based text engine; pitched as faster than TextKit 1 for large documents, but no published numbers and mixed field reports.
how_it_is_fast: TextKit 2 lays out only the viewport plus an overscroll region and estimates the rest, so opening or jumping into a large document does not lay out all preceding text. TextKit 1 lays out contiguously from the start unless noncontiguous layout is turned on.
use_it_when: Very large documents where TextKit 1's contiguous layout causes hangs on open or jump-to-line
New text views on iOS 16+ or macOS 13+ that avoid TextKit 1 compatibility mode
skip_it_when: Editors that need stable total document height or exact scroll positions, where estimated heights cause scrollbar jumps
Code that touches layoutManager, which silently switches the view back to TextKit 1
caveats: No Apple numbers; the WWDC21 claims are qualitative.
ChimeHQ's benchmark README states results in words only and ran on a macOS 14 beta.
Marcin Krzyzanowski (STTextView) reports, after four years on TextKit 2, that viewport height estimates change as more text is laid out and that TextEdit shows the same problems.
tradeoffs: Estimated layout outside the viewport makes total height and scroll offsets unstable.
Falling back to TextKit 1 compatibility mode is one-way and costly.

evidence.quote: Based on these tests, TextKit 1 is extremely fast and TextKit 2 actually even a small amount faster!
I'm using macOS 14 beta, so that may be a factor.
It was introduced in macOS 12, and I found it basically unusable.
The estimation changes frequently as I lay out more/different parts of the document.
TextEdit app from macOS suffers from the very same issues I do in my implementations.
